query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Analyze and triage Zendesk support tickets at scale: search ticket queues, enrich tickets with requester/order context, add private AI triage notes and tags, verify queues are drained, and aggregate product-support trends over a large historical ticket set.

query_ground_truth.rationale: An agent needs to query the ticketing system to find and triage tickets currently in the queue.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: Optional (if credentials uncertain) [Prerequisite]: Validate access using ZENDESK_GET_ABOUT_ME (confirm the account context before querying).
Required [Step]: Retrieve tickets lacking an assignee using ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK (query for ticket records with empty/unset assignee).
Required (if more pages indicated) [Step]: Paginate with ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK until no next page remains, accumulating results for review.
Optional (if you need more fields before action) [Step]: Fetch full ticket details using ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_TICKET_BY_ID (inspect status/priority/subject).
Optional (if assigning is required and assignee unknown) [Prerequisite]: Find the intended agent using ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_USERS (select the correct user record and capture its numeric id).
Optional (if assignment is approved) [Next Step]: Assign the ticket using ZENDESK_UPDATE_ZENDESK_TICKET (set assignee_id; re-fetch if validation needed).
Required (if ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK is too broad or insufficient) [Fallback]: List via ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_TICKETS and filter client-side where assignee_id is null.
known_pitfalls: [ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK] Very large result sets may not be practical to inspect inline; be prepared to process the returned payload structure to extract ticket fields.
[ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_USERS] User search can return multiple close matches; choosing the wrong record can assign tickets to an unintended person.
[ZENDESK_UPDATE_ZENDESK_TICKET] Requires valid numeric ticket and assignee identifiers; using a non-numeric or incorrect id can cause the update to fail.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Extract a compact review table from a large search payload already loaded into memory
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import json
payload=payload
results=payload.get("results") or payload.get("data",{}).get("results",[])
rows=[{"id":t.get("id"),"status":t.get("status"),"priority":t.get("priority"),"subject":t.get("subject")} for t in (results or [])[:20]]
print(rows)
```

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: Zendesk provides customer support software with ticketing, live chat, and knowledge base features, enabling efficient helpdesk operations and customer engagement
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=zendesk. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="zendesk") to create a connection BEFORE executing any zendesk tools.

ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK.description: Tool to search for tickets, users, organizations, and groups in Zendesk using query syntax. Use when you need to find resources across Zendesk using flexible search criteria.

query.description: The search query string. Supports Zendesk query syntax for filtering by type, status, priority, etc. Example: 'type:ticket status:open priority:urgent' or 'assignee:me status:pending'.

include.description: Sideloads to include in the response, returned as top-level arrays alongside `results`. Zendesk's search endpoint requires nested syntax: `<result_type>(<resource1>,<resource2>)`. Combine multiple result types with commas. Common sideloads: `users`, `groups`, `organizations`. A flat comma list (e.g. 'users,groups') is silently ignored by Zendesk.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Options: 'updated_at', 'created_at', 'priority', 'status', 'ticket_type'. Defaults to sorting by relevance if not specified.

per_page.description: Number of results per page. Default: 10, max: 100.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction. Options: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'desc' if not specified.

ZENDESK_GET_ABOUT_ME.description: Get information about the currently authenticated user in Zendesk. Returns only the caller's own account; to look up other users, use ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_USERS. Response nests the user object under data.owner_info.user. Useful for verifying the acting user's identity and permissions before performing bulk operations.

ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_TICKETS.description: List Zendesk tickets with pagination and filtering. Only server-side filter available is external_id; status, priority, tags, assignee_id, and date-range filters must be applied client-side. Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are ISO 8601 UTC. ticket.subject may be null — coerce to string before filtering. Attachments are not included; retrieve via ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_TICKET_BY_ID. HTTP 429 rate limit responses include Retry-After header; apply exponential backoff. Paginate by following next_page until null to avoid missing tickets.

page.description: Page number for offset pagination (1-100). Limited to first 100 pages or 10,000 records total. For larger datasets, use cursor pagination (page_size) instead.

sort_by.description: Field to sort by: 'assignee', 'assignee.name', 'created_at', 'group', 'id', 'requester', 'requester.name', 'status', 'subject', 'updated_at' Omitting sort_by provides no guaranteed ordering; set explicitly when ticket order matters.

per_page.description: Number of tickets per page for offset pagination (max 100). Note: page * per_page cannot exceed 10,000. Set to 100 for large accounts to minimize requests before client-side filtering.

page_size.description: Number of tickets per page for cursor pagination (max 100). Use this for large datasets instead of page/per_page.

page_after.description: Cursor value to retrieve the next page of results. Obtained from previous response's 'after_cursor' or 'next' link.

page_before.description: Cursor value to retrieve the previous page of results. Obtained from previous response's 'before_cursor' or 'prev' link.
